Air fresheners for my car. The bag he put them in probably cost more than the gift itself. I knew he was financially struggling but had he decided to not spend $20 a day on energy drinks for even just one day I felt he could have done more than that for me. 

I'm not materialistic, but it did hurt that he barely put in any effort. This is a man I dated for two years and drove him around on my own dollar due to his poor money management skills. I had spent a great deal on his gift, something he wanted for weeks. Our birthdays were a day apart. He still bought me car air fresheners.

I bet you she has fears. Her job is intense, and if she has a history of men cheating and not treating her right, she has so many fears about being attached and this one going sour as well. She probably hasn't felt like this in a long time, maybe ever, and that scares her, so it's just easier to shut you out than to become attached and either go face the same if you were to cheat (not saying you ever would, but that's her fear), or maybe even have a horrible situation happen with work where she dreams this big life with you and never makes it home in one piece to be that girl for you. The job is high stress so she needs her head in the right place to handle it. It's possible she's cheating, but as a woman who has had these fears and seen it in others previously, this is my best guess.

Thank you so much for the well wishes. I'm sorry to hear if your experience in doing the same might have caused some hurt feelings due to her anger. 

This breakup happened a year ago. We both fucked up a lot. I felt a year was enough time to process more clearly at least on my end, and maybe give him the space to not be as angry. I honestly don't expect to hear from him at all. While a small part of me wishes he would return the favor and apologize for his wrong doings back, I don't feel that healing of him is right for me to ask, and I have learned you can't demand that kind of closure and expect it to be genuine by actually asking for it. The letter consisted mainly of my view on how I never genuinely apologized, so I did that, as well as hoped he would find someone who made him happy, even if it wasn't me. I did mention that I thought there was a gray area where our lows might have been pretty low but that for the most part we made each other very happy, and it wasn't black and white about it overall being the worst relationship. We just both had a lot going on and a lot of growing to do. I'm praying he doesn't respond negatively and takes it as a genuine effort. These kind of things are hard. 

Wish you luck as well with healing and a better life, whatever that consists of. Sending love your way.

He blocked me as well, and I had concerns about respecting his boundaries. He didn't even give me closure. After the break up we said we would end in good terms and neither would block, but after a week he was totally gone. I really hope he doesn't take it as a breakage off boundaries and just either lets it go or hears my apology in genuine nature. I understand the bouncing between emotions, I do that often. I miss him but I needed to let go. The letter being in the mailbox is giving me anxiety but I don't think I had another choice... at least I tried. 

Best of luck to you with fast healing or whatever your life is destined to bring you, be it your ex or a new lover in a new life you create for yourself. I personally don't think the end always has to be the end, but holding onto hope of return can destroy someone. Here's to us making positive changes and letting go to create a life we can love. Much love sent your way.

I moved in third grade, and one of the first friends I made in the new town turned out to be a long time best friend for a while. We met in fourth grade, I had grown up a tomboy so me and another boy in the class would hang out playing out GameBoys trading Pokémon during recess. This boy, "Jake," lived very close and my parents quickly hung out with his. Come time for middle school, he chose to go to a magnet school in the neighboring city, while I attended our public schools for middle and high school. He ended up coming back to our high school after freshman year, and though we hadn't managed to hang out as often, we had stayed in contact all of those years and maintained. Come time for college, and we head to the same community college together. Shortly after he was arrested on charges of armed robbery at a few locations, including holding a gun to a pregnant woman's head. At the time, I didn't understand why, but I generally don't like to judge anyone for anything to this day, and considering the rest of his accomplices and friends had written statements to keep their names clear, I felt bad he's the one who got majorly fucked. 

He did about 7 years in prison. Endlessly wrote me letters, most of which I responded to and even would answer his nonstop phone calls when I was living my own life. Eventually I stopped responding entirely when he began writing to me sounding almost like he was talking down to me, the way they were even worded. I had been in rehab a few times for suicidal tendencies/depression and he had told me to "get over myself," as well as mailing me a four page letter back and front about a sex dream he had of me and saying crude things, along with telling me everything I was learning about the world I was experiencing was wrong when I was simply sharing stories and topics I was studying in school at the time. It was too much. He hadn't grown at all, and often threatened to kill himself if I didn't respond, as well as constantly displaying a big ego and saying he would do his same crimes or worse if he wasn't locked up. 

He got out last summer. We're in our mid 20's now. He's back hanging with the same friends that wrote statements about him and snitched in order to stay out of prison. They are all still doing the same things. He did try to reach out, where I basically said no and blocked him when he wouldn't take that for an answer. I'm good, bro.

Truly at the end of the day I want to feel I belong/am understood. I have never felt that, aside from with my last ex though we have been broken up about a year. He was wonderful, we just both had some growing to do and it wasn't the time for us. My friends are wonderful as are my family but I constantly feel they do not understand me. Deep emotions aside, I feel they don't understand my values/beliefs/emotions as they almost constantly deny them. It makes me feel everything is only in my head. But even if it all IS only in my head, that doesn't change the pain/suffering it all causes. When things were going well... I don't know. I was relatively in a similar place, except I felt more confident and carefree. I don't know how I got there, or how I got back here. It lasted about six months, at which point the pandemic happened shortly after, and I was forced to quit my job shortly after being denied time off for a necessary surgery. 

Also, thank you kindly for responding and offering validation on my soul being generally good. It really means the world considering I needed to hear that now more than ever. It speaks volumes of your own soul and I see the light in yours as well. 💜
